facts_of_case: The parties were married in 2007. The respondent filed for divorce due to matrimonial discord. Despite service, the appellant did not appear and an ex parte decree was passed on 02.09.2009. The appellant then filed an application under Order 9 Rule 13 CPC to set aside the ex parte decree, which was dismissed.

legal_principles.principle: A marriage which is null and void is no marriage in the eye of law.
legal_principles.held: It is well settled that a marriage which is null and void is no marriage in the eye of law.

legal_principles.principle: A marriage may validly be solemnized between any two Hindus, subject to certain conditions.
legal_principles.held: Under Section 5 of the Hindu Marriage Act, a marriage may validly be solemnized between any two Hindus, subject to the following conditions:—

legal_principles.principle: A marriage solemnized after the commencement of this Act shall be null and void if it contravenes any one of the conditions specified in clauses (i), (iv) and (v) of Section 5.
legal_principles.held: Any marriage solemnized after the commencement of this Act shall be null and void and may, on a petition presented by either party thereto, against the other party, be so declared by a decree of nullity if it contravenes any one of the conditions specified in clauses (i), (iv) and (v) of Section 5.

outcome.final_order: The appeal was dismissed and the order of the trial court was upheld.

keywords: Latin maxim: Falsus in uno, falsus in omnibus
use_for_drafting: responding to applications for setting aside ex parte decrees
